newsitem.title: JAPAN: New laptop takes the anguish out of spilled coffee.
newsitem.headline: New laptop takes the anguish out of spilled coffee.

text.p: A line of notebook computers to be launched in Japan this month can stand up to traditional office enemies, including the desk-top cup of coffee, its maker said on Friday.
"Coffee spilled on the keyboard or that falls from a desk will not spell the end for this tough lines of laptops," Matsushita Electric Industrial Co said in a statement.
They can also survive being dropped from heights of up to 70 cm (28 inches).

Built to resist vibration, dust and moisture, the new Panasonic brand models are enclosed in a magnesium alloy cabinet and are three times as vibration-resistant as Matsushita's conventional models, the company said.
The hard disk drive is mounted in a shock-absorbing gel and its liquid crystal display screen protected by internal dampers.
The machines will be available in Japan under the series name ProNote FG from October 20 at prices from 398,000 yen ($3,585) to 498,000 yen ($4,486).
The company said it started selling the laptops in North America and parts of Europe as the Panasonic CF-25 last month, though without a media announcement.
Combined annual production will be 20,000 units, it said. ($l=111 yen)
